engine: Netrani Python heuristic engine v0.1.0 (offline mode)

results.title: Compile-time instrumentation breaks when -toolexec chain contains multiple wrappers
results.ground_truth_rationale: The `-toolexec` chaining panic is a real, reproducible defect. When two wrapper executables are composed via `-toolexec`, the inner instrumentation pass misinterprets the outer wrapper's `os.Args[1]` as the actual compiler path and does not propagate the secondary toolexec argument. The failure site is `instrumenter.go:183` where `args[0]` is blindly forwarded without checking for chained invocations. No commit on `main` resolves this; it is tracked as maintainer issue #973.

results.title: AST rewriter produces invalid Go syntax when function has named return with blank identifier
results.ground_truth_rationale: The blank identifier in named return positions is a genuine edge case in Go's AST that the rewriter does not handle. The issue is in the AST transformation pass that appends span variable declarations without checking for `_` (blank identifier) in the existing named return list, leading to a shadowed blank that triggers `_ declared and not used`. This is a real defect confirmed by reproducing against v0.1.0-alpha.3 — no fix exists on main.

results.title: go generate panics on interface method with variadic parameter in instrumented package
results.ground_truth_rationale: This variadic method panic was fixed in commit `a3f9e2c` (merged to `main`) which added a bounds-check guard before accessing `params[1]` in the AST rewriter's parameter-list walker. The fix was released in v0.1.0-alpha.2. Issue reporters using v0.1.0-alpha.1 will hit this, but the defect no longer exists on `main`.

results.title: Instrumentation generates duplicate import of `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace`
results.ground_truth_rationale: The duplicate import bug was resolved in commit `b7d4f19` on `main`, which added an import deduplication pass to the AST import injector before writing out the instrumented source file. The fix checks the existing import specs and skips adding an import path that is already present.

results.title: Compile instrumentation fails on cgo files: `cgo: C source files not allowed when not using cgo`
results.ground_truth_rationale: The cgo file filtering bug was addressed in commit `c2e8a41` on `main`. The fix adds a file-extension filter in the toolexec dispatch layer that separates `.c`, `.s`, and other non-Go source files from the instrumentation path, passing them directly to the underlying compiler without transformation.

results.title: Type mismatch: `context.Context` vs `*context.emptyCtx` causes instrumentation to skip function
results.ground_truth_rationale: Code inspection of the type-checking pass in `pkg/inst-api/instrumenter/type_checker.go:94-118` shows that the type resolver performs an interface satisfaction check (`implements(paramType, contextInterface)`) before the concrete-type comparison. The `*context.emptyCtx` warning message is misleading log output from an older debug path but the actual instrumentation decision is made after the interface check succeeds. Spans ARE emitted correctly; the warning is cosmetic noise from a leftover debug log. The failure mode (missing spans) is statically impossible given the current code path.

results.title: Panic on nil TraceProvider when OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true
results.ground_truth_rationale: Inspection of `pkg/inst-api-semconv/instrumenter/instrumenter.go:47-71` shows that the global tracer is initialised via `otel.GetTracerProvider()` which always returns the global no-op provider when the SDK is disabled — it never returns nil. The `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` environment variable is handled at the SDK level, not at the instrumentation layer. The panic path at the reported address cannot be reached because the `tracer` field is always set to a non-nil no-op tracer in the constructor. The reporter likely had a custom `SetTracerProvider(nil)` call elsewhere in their test harness.

results.title: Instrumented binary produces wrong span name for HTTP handler registered with chi router
results.ground_truth_rationale: This is a genuine, unresolved defect. The HTTP server instrumentation's span naming logic reads `r.URL.Path` (the resolved path) rather than querying the router's route pattern. For `chi`, the pattern is available via `chi.RouteContext(r.Context()).RoutePattern()`. The current instrumentation pass has no router-specific extraction logic. The defect is confirmed by code inspection of `pkg/inst-api-semconv/instrumenter/http.go` — no chi route-pattern extraction exists. No fix is present on `main`.

results.title: Instrumentation fails to compile when struct embeds unexported type from another package
results.ground_truth_rationale: This is a confirmed defect. The AST type-emission pass in the instrumentation pipeline does not check whether embedded struct fields are exported before emitting their fully-qualified name in the generated source. Go prohibits using unexported types from external packages as embedded fields in generated source files in a different package. The failure is reproducible and no fix exists on `main`.

results.title: Race condition: concurrent go build invocations corrupt shared instrumentation cache
results.ground_truth_rationale: This race condition on the shared instrumentation cache was already filed as issue #703 and is tracked in open PR #712 which implements per-process cache isolation using `os.Getpid()` as a directory name component. The root cause (unguarded shared cache writes under concurrent `go build -p N`) is identical. Issue #718 is a duplicate of #703.

results.title: `go test -count=2` with instrumented packages triggers duplicate registration panic
results.ground_truth_rationale: The duplicate `init()` registration panic was first reported in issue #681 and has an active fix in PR #688 that wraps the provider registration in a `sync.Once` guard. Issue #695 describes the exact same root cause (double-registration under `go test -count=2`) with identical stack trace fragments. This is a duplicate of #681.

results.title: Instrumentation adds incorrect span end to functions returning early via named error
results.ground_truth_rationale: Code inspection of the AST rewriter confirms that `defer span.End()` is always injected as the FIRST statement of the function body, before any user code including early returns. The `defer` keyword in Go guarantees execution even for early returns and panics. The reporter's mental model is incorrect: a `defer` placed at line N executes whenever the function exits, regardless of which return statement is taken. The failure mode (unclosed spans on early-return paths) is statically impossible given Go's `defer` semantics and the rewriter's injection strategy.

results.title: Build cache is never invalidated when instrumentation rules change between versions
results.ground_truth_rationale: This is a real defect. The toolexec wrapper does not embed any version-specific cache-busting key in the build actions, so Go's build cache treats instrumented packages as fresh across toolchain upgrades. The fix requires embedding the instrumentation toolchain version hash into the action ID so the build cache correctly invalidates stale instrumented artifacts. No such mechanism exists in the current codebase.

results.title: Instrumented gRPC unary interceptor double-counts spans when both client and server are in same process
results.ground_truth_rationale: In-process gRPC span doubling is a genuine, unresolved defect. The compile-time instrumentation injects both client-side and server-side interceptors independently, with no propagation check to detect that both sides are executing in the same process under the same trace context. Standard distributed tracing expects each side to produce one span, but the correlation protocol for same-process calls differs from network calls. No deduplication logic exists in the current codebase.

results.title: Panic: `reflect: call of reflect.Value.Interface on zero Value` in attribute extractor
results.ground_truth_rationale: The zero-Value reflect panic in the attribute extractor was fixed in commit `e5f3b88` on `main`. The fix adds a `reflect.Value.IsValid()` guard at `attribute_extractor.go:83` before calling `.Interface()`. The v0.0.9 release predates this fix; v0.1.0 and later are safe.

results.title: Instrumentation silently skips generic functions (type parameters)
results.ground_truth_rationale: Generic function instrumentation is a confirmed, open defect. The AST walker in the instrumentation pass uses `*ast.FuncDecl` matching which does not handle `*ast.FuncDecl.Type.TypeParams` (the Go 1.18+ generics field). The walker skips any function with a non-nil TypeParams list, resulting in zero instrumentation. No fix exists on main; this requires a separate code path for generic function instantiations.

results.title: Span attributes missing `http.request.body.size` when body is `http.NoBody`
results.ground_truth_rationale: This missing attribute for no-body requests was already reported in issue #561 with a pending fix in PR #571 that adds a `if req.Body == nil || req.Body == http.NoBody` branch to set `http.request.body.size = 0`. Issue #579 describes an identical symptom and root cause (the extractor's body-size computation skips the nil/NoBody case). This is a duplicate of #561.

results.title: OTLP exporter connection error causes instrumented binary to hang on shutdown
results.ground_truth_rationale: This is a confirmed, open defect. The shutdown path in the instrumented binary's `otelShutdown()` function calls `exporter.Shutdown(ctx)` but the context passed is created with `context.Background()` rather than the caller's deadline-bounded context, allowing the exporter's connection retry loop to run forever. No fix exists on main; the defect is reproducible by pointing the exporter at a black-hole address.
